items.title: Mozambique: 2nd edition of the Welding Olympics culminates in national award ceremony
items.summary: The Welding Olympics serve as a strategic platform to elevate technical-vocational education and welding skills, connecting youth, trainers, and professionals directly with companies operating across the oil and gas, construction, and metalworking sectors In this 2nd edition, the initiative expanded its geographic reach through competitions held in Maputo and Cabo Delgado, involving 29 participants from 10 public and private institutions, including four women. The execution in Cabo Delgado received official recognition from the Provincial Government, reinforcing the national footprint of the project and its alignment with a strategic region for the country’s energy development Opening the event, the Secretary of State for Technical-Vocational Education, Leo Elias Jamal, highlighted the importance of viewing the competition as a bridge for recognizing and scaling national talent. Frederico P.

items.title: Canada to support 200 Mozambican SMEs
items.summary: Maputo, 16 Oct (AIM) – The Canadian government, through its initiative “Trade for Resilient, Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Growth” (TRISEG), will support 200 Mozambican small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), focusing on strengthening business competitiveness, export capacity, digital transformation and climate resilience. The project, which is expected to cover 60 percent of businesses owned or led by women, is Funded by Global Affairs Canada (GAC) and implemented by TFO Canada in partnership with the Mozambique’s Institute for the Promotion of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (IPEME). TRISEG is a regional initiative to Empower SMEs in Developing Countries. In Africa, it covers eight countries: Mozambique, Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Kenya, Madagascar, Nigeria, Senegal and Zambia. Speaking at the project launch ceremony, Pascale Thivierge, Head of Cooperation at the High Commission of Canada in Mozambique, reaffirmed Canada’s commitment to strengthening economic and trade relations with Mozambique.

items.title: Revenue from LNG is for current development and future generations – Finance Minister
items.summary: Maputo, 16 Oct (AIM) – The Mozambican Government has stressed that revenue from liquefied natural gas (LNG) production will be used both to finance the country’s current development and to create wealth for future generations. “The Mozambican Government’s objective is indeed to ensure that revenue from natural gas can generate intergenerational wealth. The Sovereign Wealth Fund Law is already producing tangible results by establishing a division of LNG revenue between public expenditure and savings”, said Carla Loveira, Finance Minister. “We do not want all the resources to be entirely consumed by the current budget”, she added. Under the model currently in force, around 60 percent of revenue is channelled to the State Budget, while the remaining 40 percent goes into a savings account managed by the Bank of Mozambique. According to the minister, the funds are already financing major infrastructure projects.

items.title: The EU wants an AI revolution. But on whose terms?
items.summary: As the US and China race ahead, the European Union seeks to boost its economy with AI. Can it compete while protecting workers, safety and the climate? Step-dancers spun across the circular stage in the middle of a dark hall, entrancing an audience of policymakers and tech bosses. Not simply another bureaucratic conference, the International AI Summit , hosted in Dublin this week, aspired to something more spectacular — a grand announcement that Europe is ready for its artificial intelligence (AI) revolution Among the more than 1,500 expected guests were Google DeepMind co-founder and chair Demis Hassabis and Microsoft president Brad Smith, in addition to high-ranking European Union and Irish officials .

items.title: Mozambique: Operation Smile conducts cleft surgeries for dozens of patients at Nampula Central Hospital
items.summary: This is the third cleft surgery campaign organised by Operation Smile at Nampula Central Hospital in 2026 to correct the congenital malformation, following 17 surgical procedures in February and 20 in April, Nilza Ferrão, the NGO’s programme coordinator in Mozambique, told Lusa According to Ferrão, the current campaign is expected to benefit 44 patients, helping to reduce the province’s waiting list. “We assessed 56 patients and 44 were scheduled to take part in this campaign,” she said The surgeries cover patients aged between 12 months and 50 years from different districts of Nampula province, who were selected following clinical assessments to determine their suitability for surgery Cleft lip and cleft palate are congenital conditions that occur when the tissues forming the upper lip or the roof of the mouth (palate) do not join together completely during foetal development. They can occur separately or together.

items.title: Dad fined after son, 2, died in Cyprus hotel fall
items.summary: Joshua Foster "lost control" of his son after placing him on a windowsill, a court in Cyprus heard A father whose two-year-old boy fell from a fourth floor window at a hotel in Cyprus has been fined €3,000 (£2,500) for causing his death Joshua Foster thought the window was closed when he placed his son on a sill to show him the view of a waterpark and "lost control" of him , Paphos District Court previously heard The toddler fell nearly 40ft (12.1m) at the five-star King Evelthon Beach Hotel and Resort on 12 July, the first day of the family's holiday in Chlorakas Foster, 37, from Essex, admitted causing death through a reckless, rash or dangerous act and was sentenced on Friday morning He told reporters afterwards: "Thank you for the support.

items.title: Starlink: How Elon Musk's company influences geopolitics
items.summary: Designed to bring internet access to remote regions, Elon Musk's Starlink has become vital in crisis regions and war zones. But Ukraine also shows the risks of depending on the service Lack of internet access is a major problem in many regions of the world today Starlink was initially developed by the American tech billionaire Elon Musk to solve this problem. It was designed as a way of quickly getting the internet into regions all over the world where this was either impossible to do by conventional methods, or so expensive that it wasn't worth attempting Since then, Starlink's field of application has widened significantly. It's used as a means of communication in disaster zones, but also by armies or protest movements, for example in regions where the existing internet has been destroyed by enemy fire or shut down by authoritarian governments But there is a downside: Ukraine's military, for example, is heavily dependent on Musk's satellite system.
